description: Composite two-panel figure combining a diffraction pattern with a property plot. (a) Stacked (vertically offset) XRD profiles of 4Al, 6Al, 8Al and 10Al steels, plotted as Intensity (a.u.) on a 0-20000 y-axis against 2θ (°) from 40 to 100; the legend from bottom to top reads 4Al (black), 6Al (red), 8Al (blue), 10Al (green). Reflections are indexed (111)γ, (110)α, (200)γ, (220)γ and (211)α, with the (110)α peak dominant at the highest Al contents. Printed on each trace are the phase mass fractions: 4Al = 0%α / 100%γ, 6Al = 3.0%α / 97.0%γ, 8Al = 75.7%α / 24.3%γ, 10Al = 98.1%α / 1.9%γ. (b) Microhardness (HV) versus Al content (wt%) from 4 to 10, with two error-bar series: α-ferrite (red circles) and γ-austenite (black squares). The α curve begins only at 6 wt% Al (no ferrite in 4Al), lying between the 240 and 270 HV gridlines, and climbs to just below the 330 HV gridline at 10 wt% Al; the γ curve rises from the 150 HV gridline at 4 wt% to just under 210 HV at 10 wt%. Together the panels show that rising Al converts austenite to ferrite and that the ferrite is the harder phase.

observations.observation: Panel (a) shows four vertically offset XRD traces labelled 4Al (black), 6Al (red), 8Al (blue) and 10Al (green) over 2θ = 40-100°.
Reflections in (a) are indexed as (111)γ, (110)α, (200)γ, (220)γ and (211)α, so both austenite (γ) and ferrite (α) are present in the Al-bearing steels.
The (110)α peak becomes the strongest reflection at 8Al and 10Al, consistent with ferrite becoming the majority phase.
In (b) the α-ferrite hardness series has no data point at 4 wt% Al, consistent with the 0%α fraction printed for 4Al in (a).
In (b) the α-ferrite hardness rises from between the 240 and 270 HV gridlines at 6 wt% Al to just below the 330 HV gridline at 10 wt% Al.
In (b) the γ-austenite hardness increases only from about the 150 HV gridline (4 wt% Al) to just below 210 HV (10 wt% Al), a much smaller rise than for ferrite.
Both series in (b) carry vertical error bars, indicating scatter in the microhardness measurements.
Caption states the figure presents XRD profiles and microhardness of 4Al, 6Al, 8Al and 10Al steels, with (a) showing the aluminum content effect on phase fraction and (b) the effect on microhardness.
The citing text states the ferrite mass fractions are 75.7 % and 98.1 % for the 8Al and 10Al steels, matching the values printed in panel (a).
The citing text states that the microhardness of ferrite is significantly higher than that of austenite, so ferrite acts as a strengthening phase in the designed steels.
The abstract states the microstructure evolves with increasing Al from a single austenite phase steel at 4 %Al to a ferrite-based duplex steel at 8 %Al, nearly fully ferritic at 10 %Al.

subfigures.description: Stacked XRD profiles of 4Al, 6Al, 8Al and 10Al steels with 2θ from 40 to 100° and Intensity (a.u.) 0-20000; peaks labelled (111)γ, (110)α, (200)γ, (220)γ, (211)α and phase mass fractions printed on each trace (0/100, 3.0/97.0, 75.7/24.3, 98.1/1.9 % of α/γ).

Microhardness (HV) versus Al content (wt%) for α-ferrite (red circles) and γ-austenite (black squares) with error bars; the α series starts at 6 wt% Al and rises steeply to ~10 wt% Al, while γ rises only modestly from 4 to 10 wt% Al.

panel (b): no numeric data labels are printed; individual hardness values can only be located relative to the 150/180/210/240/270/300/330 HV gridlines
